answer: An agent economy can make high-value actions depend on a bond locked for a fixed period, then slash it when independent, randomly assigned auditors verify a fraud proof. Auditors stake too, and rewards come from the slashed bond, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and risks losing those funds if any claim is caught. Making identities cheap does not help: splitting one stake across a mesa of accounts leaves less weight per account, while copying an echo of another agent’s work cannot manufacture bonded capital. A ferrous audit trail records the result for later challenges.
